title: Google fined €890m by EU for favouring its own apps over rivals
facts: The European Union fined Google 890 million euros for favouring its own applications and services over rivals.
The 890 million euro fine is the first major enforcement action taken against Google under the Digital Markets Act.
Google's president of global affairs is Kent Walker.
The European Commission imposed a 460 million euro fine on Google for giving its own flight and hotel booking services priority in search results.
The European Commission imposed a 430 million euro penalty on Google regarding its Play Store marketplace rules.
Teresa Ribera serves as the European Union's competition chief.
Henna Virkkunen serves as the European Union tech chief.
Zach Meyers serves as director of research at the Centre on Regulation in Europe.
The European Commission moved forward with the fine following recurring tariff threats from US President Donald Trump.
Google was granted a 60-day window to comply with the European Union regulations or contest the fine in court.
The Digital Markets Act is a European Union law designed to limit the market power of major technology companies.
Google previously received billions of euros in fines from European regulators over separate antitrust and competition cases.
Kent Walker stated that compliance would require removing instant pricing and direct availability features for European users.
EU regulators stated that Google Play Store rules restricted users from being shown cheaper external offers.
EU competition chief Teresa Ribera stated that products should succeed based on quality rather than search engine ownership.
